item.title: PostgreSQL Indexing Strategies in 2026: B-tree vs GIN vs BRIN vs Hash
item.description: I once inherited a Postgres table with 40 million rows and a query that took 11 seconds to return a handful of matches. There was an index on the column being filtered. The index was just the wrong type — a B-tree sitting on a JSONB column that needed a GIN index, doing sequential-scan-adjacent work because it couldn’t actually help with the containment query being run against it. Swapping the index type, not adding more indexes, took that query from 11 seconds to 40 milliseconds.
